name: Transformer & Attention
simple_definition: The neural network architecture powering modern LLMs. Instead of reading words one-by-one in sequence, it processes the entire sentence at once and uses Self-Attention to calculate how much each word relates to every other word.
analogy: Imagine reading a textbook with a highlighter. Instead of reading blindly word-by-word, attention highlights which clues belong together—like connecting the word 'it' back to 'the dog' three sentences earlier.
why_it_matters: Before Transformers (2017), models like RNNs forgot the beginning of long texts. Transformers parallelize training on GPUs and handle massive context windows.
math_intuition: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q·Kᵀ / √d_k) · V. Queries look for Keys; when they match, they pull values.

name: Latent Space & Embeddings
simple_definition: A high-dimensional mathematical map where computers convert words, images, or audio into arrays of numbers (vectors). Items with similar meanings end up close together in this space.
analogy: Think of a magical 3D library where every book floats. Mystery novels cluster on one side, cookbooks on the other. Distance equals conceptual difference.
why_it_matters: Computers cannot read letters; they only calculate numbers. Vector embeddings let machines perform arithmetic on human ideas (e.g. King - Man + Woman ≈ Queen).
math_intuition: Words are projected into an n-dimensional space (e.g., 1536 dimensions) where cosine similarity measures semantic closeness.

name: Model Quantization
simple_definition: Compressing an AI model by reducing the numerical precision of its weights—typically converting 16-bit floating point numbers (FP16) down to 8-bit or 4-bit integers (INT8/INT4).
analogy: Like converting an uncompressed 50MB RAW image into a crisp 2MB JPEG. You save 90% of the storage and memory with almost no visible loss in quality.
why_it_matters: A 70B parameter model in FP16 takes 140GB of VRAM (requiring expensive enterprise GPUs). Quantized to 4-bit, it runs on a single 48GB workstation or consumer PC.
math_intuition: Mapping continuous 16-bit floats to discrete small integer bins using a scaling factor: W_quant = round(W / scale) + zero_point.

name: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
simple_definition: An architecture where a large model is split into dozens of smaller specialized sub-networks ('experts'). A router decides which 1 or 2 experts activate for each specific token.
analogy: Instead of one person answering every hospital question, a triage receptionist routes cardiology questions to the cardiologist and fracture questions to the radiologist.
why_it_matters: Gives you the knowledge capacity of an enormous 600B+ model while only paying the compute cost of a 40B model during generation (used by Mixtral, Grok, and Gemini).
math_intuition: y = Σ G(x)ᵢ · Eᵢ(x), where G(x) is a sparse softmax gating network activating only top-k experts.

name: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
simple_definition: Connecting an LLM to an external search engine or private database so it retrieves real-time facts and injects them into the prompt before generating an answer.
analogy: Taking an open-book exam. Instead of relying solely on whatever facts the student memorized months ago, they look up the exact company manual or syllabus before answering.
why_it_matters: Drastically slashes hallucinations, avoids expensive model retraining for new data, and keeps company proprietary information private.
math_intuition: Query vector Q retrieves top-K documents via k-Nearest Neighbors; context is prepended: Prompt = Context + Q.

name: LoRA & PEFT Fine-Tuning
simple_definition: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes the original massive neural network and only trains tiny adapter matrices inserted into specific layers, reducing trainable weights by over 99%.
analogy: Adding transparent sticky notes with corrections into an encyclopedia instead of republishing and printing the entire multi-volume book from scratch.
why_it_matters: Allows college researchers and indie developers to fine-tune giant models on a single consumer GPU instead of renting a cluster of 8x H100s.
math_intuition: Decomposing weight update ΔW of size d×k into two low-rank matrices B(d×r) and A(r×k) where rank r << min(d, k).

name: KV Cache (Key-Value Cache)
simple_definition: A memory optimization technique that stores previously computed Key and Value matrices of past tokens during text generation, avoiding re-calculating attention over the whole prompt.
analogy: Taking meeting notes as you talk. When someone says a new sentence, you just append it, rather than listening to the entire recording of the meeting from minute one.
why_it_matters: Without KV Cache, generating a 1,000-token response would require O(N²) quadratic calculations. KV cache makes inference O(N) linear in time.
math_intuition: Past K and V vectors are held in GPU VRAM buffer; each new token only needs 1 row of Q multiplied against cached K and V.

name: Temperature & Top-p (Nucleus)
simple_definition: Sampling hyperparameters that determine how predictable or creative an LLM's next token choice will be. Low temp picks the most likely word; high temp explores rarer words.
analogy: A spice slider on a recipe. At 0.0, the chef strictly follows the exact traditional dish. At 1.0, the chef tosses in adventurous, exotic spices.
why_it_matters: For code or math, you want temperature near 0 for accuracy. For storytelling or brainstorming, you want temperature 0.7–0.9 for creative variety.
math_intuition: Softmax logits are divided by T: P(w) = exp(z_i / T) / Σ exp(z_j / T). As T→0, distribution sharpens into argmax.

name: RLHF & DPO Alignment
simple_definition: Techniques used after pretraining to teach raw language models to be helpful, polite, harmless, and follow instructions based on human ratings (Direct Preference Optimization).
analogy: A driving instructor sitting next to a teen driver giving praise for gentle stops and pointing out reckless swerving, shaping their natural habits into safe driving.
why_it_matters: A raw pretrained LLM just predicts the next internet word (including scams, profanity, and rambling). Alignment turns it into a helpful conversational assistant like Claude or ChatGPT.
math_intuition: DPO bypasses complex reinforcement learning by directly optimizing the implicit reward: max log σ(β log(π_θ(y_w|x) / π_ref(y_w|x)) - β log(π_θ(y_l|x) / π_ref(y_l|x))).

name: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
simple_definition: Prompting or training models to generate intermediate reasoning tokens step-by-step before producing their final conclusion, mimicking human deliberate thinking.
analogy: Writing down your rough work in the margins of a math exam instead of trying to multiply 4-digit numbers entirely in your head.
why_it_matters: Standard LLMs allocate the same amount of compute to '2+2' as they do to a complex quantum theorem. CoT (and reasoning models like OpenAI o1/o3) scale compute at test-time.
math_intuition: Decomposing P(Answer | Question) into Σ P(Answer | Thought, Question) · P(Thought | Question).

name: Diffusion Models
simple_definition: Generative models (used in Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and Sora) that learn to generate images/videos by progressively removing gaussian noise from an image step-by-step.
analogy: A sculptor starting with a messy block of marble and progressively chiseling away tiny rough grains until a detailed masterpiece emerges.
why_it_matters: Replaced GANs (Generative Adversarial Networks) because diffusion is far more stable to train and creates photorealistic imagery without mode collapse.
math_intuition: Forward process adds noise: q(x_t | x_{t-1}). Neural network learns reverse conditional distribution p_θ(x_{t-1} | x_t) to predict and subtract noise.

name: Gradient Descent & Backprop
simple_definition: The foundational optimization algorithm of all deep learning. Backpropagation calculates the error gradient with calculus chain-rule, and gradient descent adjusts weights to minimize loss.
analogy: A hiker lost in dense fog on a mountain trying to find the valley floor by taking small steps in whichever direction slopes steepest downward.
why_it_matters: Every modern AI system—from tiny perceptrons to frontier LLMs—learns by calculating these gradients millions of times over billions of tokens.
math_intuition: Weight update rule: W_{t+1} = W_t - η · ∇L(W_t), where η is the learning rate and ∇L is the partial derivative vector.

name: Overfitting vs Generalization
simple_definition: When a model memorizes the training data including random noise, performing perfectly on training examples but failing miserably on unseen test data.
analogy: A student who memorizes the exact answer numbers of yesterday's practice test, but fails the real exam because the numbers changed slightly.
why_it_matters: The ultimate goal of machine learning is generalization to the real world, prevented via dropout, weight decay, data augmentation, and early stopping.
math_intuition: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff: Total Error = Bias² + Variance + Irreducible Noise. High variance corresponds to overfitting.

name: Context Window & Needle-in-a-Haystack
simple_definition: The maximum number of tokens an LLM can read and hold in its attention buffer simultaneously in a single prompt session.
analogy: The physical surface area of your desk. A 4K context desk only fits a single essay; a 1M context desk fits an entire 10-volume encyclopedia.
why_it_matters: Long context allows analyzing full codebases, books, and financial reports, but models can suffer from 'lost in the middle' where they overlook facts buried in long text.
math_intuition: Standard attention memory scales O(N²) without sparse or flash attention; RoPE (Rotary Position Embeddings) scales context length.

name: AI Agents & Function Calling
simple_definition: Systems where an LLM is given tools (calculators, web browsers, bash terminals, APIs) and operates in a loop: perceive → plan → execute tool → evaluate output → finish.
analogy: Transitioning from an encyclopedia that can only recite facts to hiring a capable intern who can browse Google, execute code, and write reports autonomously.
why_it_matters: Moves AI from passive chatbots to active autonomous problem solvers capable of building software, analyzing stocks, and operating complex systems.
math_intuition: ReAct framework: Thought → Action → Observation loop until stopping condition 'Final Answer' is reached.

name: Cosine Similarity
simple_definition: A metric that measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors, checking whether they point in roughly the same direction regardless of their vector magnitude.
analogy: Two people pointing their fingers across a room. If both point toward the same window, their angle is 0° (similarity = 1.0), even if one person's arm is longer.
why_it_matters: The core mathematical operation used by vector search engines, semantic caching, recommendation systems, and RAG retrieval pipelines.
math_intuition: cos(θ) = (A · B) / (||A|| · ||B||) = Σ(AᵢBᵢ) / (√ΣAᵢ² · √ΣBᵢ²). Range: -1 (opposite) to +1 (identical direction).

name: FlashAttention & IO-Awareness
simple_definition: An exact attention algorithm that reorganizes GPU memory access into fast SRAM tiles, avoiding slow HBM read/writes and speeding up attention by 2-4x with zero approximation.
analogy: Organizing cooking ingredients on the counter right beside the stove instead of walking back and forth to the pantry for every pinch of salt.
why_it_matters: Made training 32K–128K context models computationally feasible on modern GPUs (A100/H100) and powers vLLM and TensorRT-LLM.
math_intuition: Tiling Q, K, V blocks in GPU SRAM; uses online softmax renormalization to avoid writing N×N attention matrix to GPU HBM.

name: Mamba & State Space Models (SSM)
simple_definition: A linear-time alternative to Transformers. It uses selective state-space equations to process sequences in O(N) linear time and constant memory instead of quadratic O(N²).
analogy: A tape recorder updating a summary notepad in real-time as an interview progresses, rather than pausing to re-read the entire tape after every single word.
why_it_matters: Enables processing million-token sequences at lightning speeds where standard Transformer attention runs out of GPU memory.
math_intuition: h'(t) = A·h(t) + B·x(t), y(t) = C·h(t). Discretized using Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) with selective input-dependent parameters B, C, and Δ.

name: Speculative Decoding
simple_definition: Accelerating large model generation by using a tiny draft model to guess the next 4-5 words quickly, which the large model validates in parallel in a single GPU pass.
analogy: An eager junior apprentice drafting the email outline in 2 seconds, and the senior director glancing over it to approve or adjust it in one glance.
why_it_matters: Achieves 2x–3x faster tokens-per-second generation without losing a single bit of output quality or changing the output distribution.
math_intuition: Draft model proposals {x₁...x_k} accepted with probability min(1, P_target(x) / P_draft(x)), preserving exact target model probability distribution.

name: RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding)
simple_definition: A position encoding method that rotates vector coordinates in 2D pairs to inject relative token distance directly into attention dot products.
analogy: A clock face where the minute hand rotates forward for every second of conversation, letting you measure the exact angle between any two moments.
why_it_matters: Used in LLaMA, Mistral, and Gemini. Enables models to extrapolate smoothly to much longer context windows via frequency base scaling (YaRN).
math_intuition: R_Θ,m · x_m: 2D orthogonal rotation matrix where angle is proportional to token position m and feature index i.

name: GQA (Grouped-Query Attention)
simple_definition: An attention variant where multiple query heads share a single key-value head, drastically reducing the KV cache memory size while maintaining multi-head expressive power.
analogy: Four readers sharing one reference index card instead of each reader printing their own identical copy of the card.
why_it_matters: Cuts GPU VRAM required for KV cache by up to 8x, allowing servers to handle massive batch sizes and 128k context windows simultaneously.
math_intuition: MHA has H_q queries and H_kv=H_q keys/values. GQA sets H_kv = H_q / G, sharing KV pairs across groups of G query heads.

name: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)
simple_definition: A subword tokenization algorithm that iteratively merges the most frequent pairs of characters into single tokens until reaching a target vocabulary size.
analogy: Creating shorthand abbreviations for the most common syllables in text, so frequent words like 'learning' become single symbols while rare words are broken into pieces.
why_it_matters: Balances vocabulary size against sequence length, preventing out-of-vocabulary (OOV) errors while allowing numbers, code, and multiple languages to be tokenized.
math_intuition: Statistical frequency counting: argmax_{(a,b)} Count(a, b), followed by replacing all occurrences with a new token symbol.

name: Knowledge Distillation
simple_definition: Training a compact, lightweight student model to replicate the output logits and reasoning behavior of a massive teacher model.
analogy: A master craftsman mentoring an apprentice one-on-one, teaching them their refined instincts in months instead of making them read 10,000 textbooks alone.
why_it_matters: Creates ultra-fast models that can run directly on mobile phones or edge devices (e.g. Gemini Nano, Claude Haiku, LLaMA-1B) with near-frontier performance.
math_intuition: Loss = α · CE(y_true, y_student) + (1-α) · T² · KL(Softmax(z_teacher / T) || Softmax(z_student / T)).

name: Sparse Autoencoders (SAE)
simple_definition: An interpretability technique that decomposes polysemantic neural activations into millions of monosemantic features, identifying exact concepts inside black-box models.
analogy: A prism that takes blended white sunlight and splits it into individual pure colors, revealing the exact hidden ingredients of a model's thoughts.
why_it_matters: Breakthrough in AI safety and mechanistic interpretability (pioneered by Anthropic and OpenAI) allowing researchers to find features for deception, sycophancy, or biology.
math_intuition: Reconstruct activation x via hidden features f(x) = ReLU(W_enc · x + b_enc) with L1 sparsity penalty: min ||x - W_dec · f(x)||² + λ ||f(x)||₁.
